name: Brick-based Hierarchical Storage
text:
# Brick-based Hierarchical Storage
## Overview
Brick-based Hierarchical Storage organizes volumetric data into fixed-size, non-overlapping cubic blocks (bricks) to optimize memory locality, enable efficient sparse access, and support multi-resolution rendering [G]. It addresses the memory overhead and access inefficiencies of dense voxel grids by grouping data into spatially coherent units that can be loaded, compressed, or traversed independently [G]. The family encompasses methods that use spatial partitioning for [adaptive mesh refinement](#5344-adaptive-mesh-refinement-amr-data-structures.md) [2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md], sparse page tables for voxel datasets [2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md], and compact encoding for segmentation labels [4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md] [G]. It sets itself apart from sibling [sparse structures](#5-sparse-structures.md) by explicitly partitioning space into fixed-size bricks rather than using dynamic octrees or [hash grids](#936-hash-grids.md), enabling predictable memory layouts and hardware-accelerated traversal [G].
## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [ExaBricks Hierarchy](2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md)
A rendering method for Block-Structured Adaptive Mesh Refinement (BS-AMR) data that reorganizes input cells into compact, non-overlapping bricks and builds a spatial index called Active Brick Regions (ABRs) to support smooth interpolation across level boundaries [2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md]. It is distinguished from siblings by its explicit construction of a secondary spatial index over brick support regions to enable hardware-accelerated traversal via an RTX BVH while maintaining $C^0$ continuity [2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md]. Choose this method when rendering AMR datasets that require high-quality interpolation across refinement boundaries without costly per-sample cell location kernels [2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md].

### [Sparse Page Table and Brick Pool](2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md)
A sparse volume representation that avoids materializing a dense 3D grid by using a two-level structure: a page table mapping logical $8^3$-texel regions to resident bricks, and a pool of apron-padded bricks [2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md]. It is distinguished from siblings by its explicit separation of spatial offset and page table ID within the [brick ID structure](#3192-brick-id-page-table-layout.md) and its use of a fixed-capacity brick pool with terrain occlusion handling [2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md]. Choose this method when rendering large sparse voxel datasets (up to $2048^3$) in engines like Unreal Engine, where bounding memory usage and enabling [empty-space skipping](#1002-empty-space-skipping.md) are priorities [2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md].

### [Brick ID Page Table Layout](3192-brick-id-page-table-layout.md)
A memory-efficient indexing scheme used within brick-based hierarchical volume storage to map spatial brick locations to their corresponding page tables in a multi-channel, multi-resolution environment [3192-brick-id-page-table-layout.md]. It is distinguished from siblings by its specific bit-packing of spatial offsets and page table identifiers into fixed-width 32-bit integers, explicitly separating spatial offset and page table ID [3192-brick-id-page-table-layout.md]. Choose this method when implementing GPU-resident brick caches that require deterministic, cache-friendly lookups for multi-channel volumes with up to 256 page tables [3192-brick-id-page-table-layout.md].

### [Compressed Segmentation Volume](4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md)
A [lossless compression](#5360-entropy-encoding.md) technique for voxel-based segmentation volumes that encodes individual bricks using a multi-resolution label pyramid and an iterative refinement scheme [4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md]. It is distinguished from siblings by its explicit modeling of discrete, categorical labels through parent/neighbor reuse and palette back-references, rather than treating data as continuous fields [4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md]. Choose this method when rendering large-scale segmented volumes with sharp, non-interpolating boundaries, as it significantly reduces memory bandwidth and storage requirements while supporting fast parallel decompression [4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md].

### Brick Maps
#### definition
- [S1, unofficial] A multi-resolution storage structure for 3D volume caches, analogous to 2D mipmaps, used to reduce aliasing (jiggle/noise) when rendering distant objects.
#### step
- [S1, unofficial] Create downsized versions of the original grid data by averaging 8 voxels from the previous level to form one voxel in the next level.
- [S1, unofficial] Iterate through levels n=1 to numLevels-2, where baseResolution is halved each level.
#### formula
- [S1, unofficial] The value of a voxel at level n is the average of 8 voxels from level n-1: $V_{n}(x,y,z) = 0.125 \times \sum_{i=0}^{1}\sum_{j=0}^{1}\sum_{k=0}^{1} V_{n-1}(2x+i, 2y+j, 2z+k)$
#### parameter
- [S1, unofficial] numLevels: The number of resolution levels, calculated as $\log_2(baseResolution)$.
#### pitfall
- [S1, unofficial] The downsizing process is trivial only if the grid resolution is a power of 2.
#### usage
- [S1, unofficial] Supported by production renderers and formats such as [OpenVDB](#1508-openvdb-vdb.md).

### SGGX Storage Format
#### definition
- [S2] Stores the main indices of the SGGX matrix S in leaf nodes (LoD 0) using a compact linear space representation allowing 1 byte per parameter, totaling 6 bytes per distribution.

## Background
Brick-based storage concepts originated in the context of 3D texture caching and volume rendering optimization [G]. The term "brick map" was coined by the Pixar Renderman team, adapting the 2D mipmap concept to 3D voxel grids to handle aliasing, though the exact origin is uncertain [S1, unofficial]. The approach has since been generalized to handle adaptive mesh refinement [2182-exabricks-hierarchy.md], sparse voxel datasets [2550-sparse-page-table-and-brick-pool.md], and semantic segmentation volumes [4985-compressed-segmentation-volume.md] [G].
